small_guidance:
- Add more autotune configs varying BLOCK_SP (16, 128) and try num_stages=4; also try tiling oc as well (BLOCK_OC=8 or 16 since OC=16) instead of always covering full OC, to expose more parallelism in the grid.
- The innermost `ww` loop over BLOCK_SP-wide vector loads is the hottest path; consider hoisting the `valid_d & valid_h` scalar masks out of the `ww` loop (they don't depend on ww) so only `valid_w` is recomputed per iteration.
- Consider swapping loop order so kd/kh/kw is the outer static loop and dd/hh/ww is innermost: for fixed (kd,dd) the input depth id_ = (pd*2+dd+PAD_D-kd)//STRIDE_D is one of only a couple of distinct values; precomputing per-(kd,dd) once avoids redundant divmod inside the kw loop.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an explicit GEMM: each program computes a tile of (OC) x (pooled spatial tile) by gathering an im2col-style K-dimension of IC*KD*KH*KW*8 (the 8 covering the pool window). Use tl.dot for the matmul instead of scalar outer-product accumulation; with OC=16 this still benefits from tensor-core paths if BLOCK_OC is padded to 16 and BLOCK_SP to 32+.
- Alternatively, restructure parallelism around (n, oc_tile, pooled_d, pooled_hw_tile) with input-stationary scheduling: load each input element once and scatter-contribute to up to KD*KH*KW output positions (after pooling, the relevant outputs are a small fixed set). This avoids the 8x redundant input fetches the current scheme does inside the dd/hh/ww loop.
- Switch the output (and ideally weight) layout to channels-last so the OC axis is contiguous and the final store is one coalesced write per spatial position, instead of the current strided store across OC.
